summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cerebrovascular disease, coronary artery disease, and alcohol use was admitted for chest pain and dizziness. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal troponins and EKG. The chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal. A non-contrast head CT showed no acute intracranial abnormalities, and his dizziness, described as lightheadedness, resolved with IV rehydration and was attributed to dehydration and alcohol use. He was monitored for alcohol withdrawal using the CIWA protocol and received thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamins. His tremor remained at baseline, and no new neurological deficits were found. He was discharged stable with instructions to avoid alcohol, continue all prescribed medications, and follow up with primary care, with plans for home support services.
